To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The recombination model can account for the observed v2 of multi- strange particles, but only if a substantial amount of recombination takes place after the chemical freeze-out, 2) The recombination of strange quarks is not sufficient to account for the measured v2 of the φ and Ω, 3) The recombination scenario is disfavored by the observed v2 for the Λ, 4) Hydrodynamics is able to account for the observed elliptic flow

the recombination and statistical-hadrochemistry models predict that the elliptic flow of the Ω will be much larger than the hydrodynamic model, and that the recombination model predicts a large elliptic flow of φ particles.
